races.name: Randox Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cap Bernat
runners_data.note: Veteran 13-year-old who ran well over similar distances on Good in his prime (P at 2m3f Good); Danny Mullins rides for a trainer with no recent runners, and 442 days off the track is a major concern, though his prominent style at least means he won't be shuffled back.|

runners_data.name: Eben Zaabeel
runners_data.note: A J Martin has six runners in the past fortnight but this five-year-old's form string (0-) offers little encouragement; at his core he wants to race from off the pace but the compressed rear-field means he may end up closer to the speed than suits, diluting his ability to produce a fresh finish.|

runners_data.name: Euro Agent
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's yard is in flying form (1 from 39 in 14 days) and this horse has placed at 2m3f on Good, which is the most relevant form in the field for the trip; he is a genuine hold-up type who will likely find himself in mid-division rather than at the back, meaning his late kick may arrive one position too early.|

runners_data.name: Fairy Meadow
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins sends this nine-year-old back quickly (38 days) after a fall and a pulled-up run — the fade-in-finish flag and the fall on recent record raise durability concerns; his natural rearward style is further compromised by the crowded hold-up group forcing him forward, and the limited two-run hurdles record gives little confidence.|

runners_data.name: Fox Walk
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and the pivotal horse in this race shape; trainer Noel C Kelly has one winner from 12 in 14 days, and Fox Walk's only hurdles start (3rd at 2m5f Good) shows he stays and handles the going — Torrens can dictate at will with no rival likely to push him early.|

runners_data.name: Mr Caulfield
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Fox Walk (Kelly/Kelly) and showed a placed effort at 2m1f Good, suggesting he handles conditions; his hold-up tendencies put him in the redistribution pool, but his solid form line (2-P102) makes him one of the more reliable finishers if he can travel close enough to challenge.|

runners_data.name: Tullynakill
runners_data.note: Complete unknown — no public form and no days-since-last-run figure available; J J Slevin is a high-calibre booking that must be respected, and Crawford's patient approach with young hurdlers means Tullynakill could be anything, but the going-unknown tag and light experience make him a speculative element.|

runners_data.name: Nelliestar
runners_data.note: Apprentice claim (7lb) for Paddy Cleary noted, but the form figures (08) and the consistent fade-in-finish flag paint a bleak picture; only 12 days between runs for a horse that has finished no closer than eighth in 18f-plus hurdles on Good — context suggests this is a fitness spin rather than a winning attempt.|

runners_data.name: Greenroad Girl
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at four and the lightest carried (156lbs); two runs over similar distances on Good show she can complete the course but finishing positions (P, 6th) give little encouragement, and Darragh O'Keeffe cannot conjure more natural ability than the form reflects over a trip that may already be stretching her.|

races.paceDynamic: Fox Walk is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, should dictate from the front at a tempo entirely of Simon Torrens's choosing on Good ground at Downpatrick. Behind Fox Walk, the prominent slot is thinly populated — Cap Bernat is the only other horse whose natural style places him close to the pace, meaning the leader faces no meaningful early pressure. The bulk of this field — Fairy Meadow, Eben Zaabeel, Euro Agent, Mr Caulfield, Nelliestar, and Greenroad Girl — are natural hold-up types, but with so many closers relative to available rear-field space, several will be shuffled into midfield positions that do not reflect their true racing style. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader on Good ground over 2m2f with a compacted chasing pack — clearly favours Fox Walk to set a sustainable gallop and prove hard to reel in, with any prominent or mid-division horse who travels fluently into the final circuit the likeliest beneficiary if the leader comes back to them; the field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and Eben Zaabeel, Fairy Meadow, and Euro Agent are most likely to be forced into closer positions than their natural style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fox Walk Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fox Walk bowls clear from the start and sets a controlled, sustainable pace with no rival willing or able to pressure him.
scenarios.body: Fox Walk exploits a lone-leader scenario on Good ground, controlling tempo through the final circuit and jumping his rivals into submission; Torrens can dictate the fractions and deny hold-up types the strong gallop they need to launch a meaningful late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Cap Bernat or a redistributed mid-division horse travels powerfully into contention and overcomes Fox Walk at the last.
scenarios.body: A smooth traveller from the chasing group picks up Fox Walk approaching the final hurdle where the leader's controlled pace has kept them within striking range; Good ground ensures the pace is honest enough for a prominent finisher to get competitive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fox Walk's gallop is genuinely strong enough to tire him out in the final half-mile, opening the door for true hold-up types.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected pace collapses the field together at the second-last, allowing a hold-up runner who has threaded through midfield to swoop; however, because Eben Zaabeel, Fairy Meadow, and Euro Agent are likely racing out of their natural role and further forward than ideal, the classic late-run shape is partially compromised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Incident Reshapes Race
scenarios.trigger: If a fall, refusal, or interference disrupts the natural race order and voids the expected tactical shape.
scenarios.body: A loose horse or mid-race incident bunches the field and negates Fox Walk's lead advantage, opening the contest to whoever jumps cleanly and stays out of trouble; Tullynakill, lightly raced and a complete unknown, could benefit from a messy race that equalises experience gaps.

watchPoints.text: Fox Walk — if he jumps cleanly at the first two hurdles and establishes a clear lead without pressure, the race shape locks in immediately and the outcome could be settled well before the home turn.

Eben Zaabeel, Fairy Meadow, Euro Agent — all three are natural hold-up types likely to be squeezed into mid-division; watch for traffic issues and shuffling in the first mile as the compressed field jostles for position.
Tullynakill — J J Slevin's booking on a complete unknown with no public form is the single biggest wildcard; any unexpected early move by Slevin could disrupt Fox Walk's uncontested lead scenario.

Cap Bernat — 442 days off the track is a significant flag at age 13; watch his jumping in the early stages as any hesitation or mistake would confirm he is ring-rusty and can be safely discounted from live calculations.

Fairy Meadow — the fall flag on recent record warrants monitoring at the first hurdle, particularly if the field bunches on the approach; a repeat incident could trigger mid-race chaos relevant to Scenario D.

races.name: WillWeGo.com Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ripsnorter
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here; Danny Mullins on a 5yo who won over this exact course and distance on Good last time out and is well-handicapped off OR 99, with strong similar-going form (5/7 in Good conditions) — controls this race from the front and must be respected throughout.
runners_data.comment: Ripsnorter showed he could win at this level with a victory five starts back, and he arrives on a fair freshener of 21 days having run over today's trip and going before; the concern is his three most recent efforts have all been well below that form.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin partners this hold-up type whose recent form includes a close third and second in Good-ground hurdles; excellent course-going record (14/14 in similar conditions) suggests he handles this surface well and will be finishing strongly if the pace is genuine enough.
runners_data.comment: Le Diablo shaped with promise when third three starts back and second four starts back, and he returns after 21 days refreshed, with experience over today's trip and going and a rating nudging above his official mark; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Youknowthecode
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott 4yo (1/39 T14) carrying a "fades in finish" flag and a poor recent form string of 860-0; limited similar-going experience (1/4) is a concern on Good ground and this horse's profile points firmly to one who cannot be trusted to see out the race competitively.
runners_data.comment: Youknowthecode has going experience to call on and our rating of 104 puts him third best in the field, yet he is winless in his last four starts and a trainer firing at just 3% recently is the chief concern, alongside a hefty 164 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: A 9yo veteran with Harry Sexton (7) in the plate; consistent in similar conditions (14/15) and placed four times from last five relevant runs, but the age and the 163lb burden mean he is relying on the pace to suit him late rather than any explosive change of gear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Pahlavi nevertheless shapes as the one to beat here, rated 108 and ranked top of the twelve, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; the weight of 163 lb is the one note of caution, though a 15-day turnaround keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: South Of Killerig
runners_data.note: Sheehy-trained hold-up horse with a genuine rear-of-field style; pressed into a midfield map position here because the back of the race is over-subscribed — should be noted that the horse has never won in 7 similar-going runs, and racing out of its natural role tempers its claims.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and twice pulled up in that spell, South Of Killerig arrives on a tricky note, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a 15-day turnaround leaves him fresh; the 162 lb burden is no help.

runners_data.name: Echinacea
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 4yo (only 3 runs to form) returning after 64 days; the two placed efforts came on Standard ground and the similar-going record (9/15 runs) is modest — a horse of potential but one facing the unknown, and the layoff adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Echinacea faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 64-day break carrying 161 lb.

runners_data.name: He Who Dares
runners_data.note: Won over hurdles on Good ground in a higher-rated company (1W2P from 11 similar-going runs) but carries a "fades in finish" tag and is one of several horses whose natural hold-up style puts it further back than the map suggests; Phillip Enright will need a clean trip through a crowded field to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Three unplaced runs punctuate his recent record, and a rating of 78 ranked tenth of twelve makes him hard to fancy at the weights despite a last-start win and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Menas Miracle
runners_data.note: The only other prominent type in the race beyond Ripsnorter; Mr B T Stone (7) partners a 7yo with two wins over Good hurdles (2W5P from 12 similar-going runs), and a horse who can sit close to the pace without fighting for position has a structural advantage in this particular race shape.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has since pulled up and finished third, so her form is patchy at best; has run over today's trip and going, and 17 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, though 155 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Banphrionsa Alainn
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 5yo filly with just three hurdle runs on record (0W0P) and a "fades in finish" concern; a true hold-up operator who will be navigating an even more congested space than her natural position suggests, making it hard to see how she gets competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked 11th of 12 on our figures, Banphrionsa Alainn faces a stiff task at 147 lb, though she has run over today's going before and a fifth last time out at least shows some recent engagement.

runners_data.name: Firstupbestdressed
runners_data.note: Headgear (tb) worn by this 6yo who has failed to win or place in 9 similar-going runs; the horse's instinct is to race from behind, yet the overcrowded rear forces it further forward than it wants to be — a modest profile compounded by the positional difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Firstupbestdressed does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a 12-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh, though consecutive unplaced efforts and a hefty 146 lb make the case against him equally hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness 4yo with three places from 9 similar-going runs (0W3P) who has Darragh O'Keeffe, one of the stronger jockeys in the field, in the saddle; the horse's natural hold-up profile is crowded out here, though O'Keeffe's tactical nous gives it a slightly better chance of finding a gap than most redistributed types.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but placed second two runs back and third on a couple of other recent occasions, Granlahan has experience of today's trip and going and arrives fit on a 12-day turnaround, though carrying 146 lb and ranked eighth of twelve he faces a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: John Dixen
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field (74) and a "fades in finish" flag alongside a form string of 000-60; poor similar-going record (2/6), a 41-day absence and an apprentice in the plate (Conor Clarke, 7) all point to an outsider with very limited scope to get competitive regardless of how the race is run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, John Dixen faces a stiff ask off 140 lb after 41 days away, with little in the recent form to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Ripsnorter is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner handicap hurdle and, with no genuine rival willing to seriously contest the lead, Danny Mullins can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — this is a race likely to be run at an honest but not brutal pace, preserving stamina for the closing stages over 2m2f on Good ground. The field nominally appears packed with hold-up types, but several of them — South Of Killerig, He Who Dares, Granlahan, Banphrionsa Alainn, Firstupbestdressed, and John Dixen — are true hold-up horses redistributed to the midfield map position simply because the rear is over-subscribed; the realistic midfield picture will be congested and competitive for position. Menas Miracle is the only other prominent type alongside Ripsnorter, meaning the actual front section of the race is thin and likely to produce a steady, mutualistic pace rather than one that blows the field apart. This race shape strongly favours a well-placed prominent or tracking runner who can sit just behind Ripsnorter without burning energy, pounce approaching the last, and resist a one-paced challenge from closers who have spent the race navigating a congested midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ripsnorter Controls, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter bowls along at a fair but uncontested clip and a handy tracker sits poised to strike from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Ripsnorter sets a controlled tempo with Menas Miracle close by, creating a race where the horse quickest to accelerate off that steady pace wins; horses with the tactical speed to sit within two lengths of the leader and pick up immediately are ideally positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Closers Close Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter sets a genuinely slow early gallop that compresses the field and allows hold-up horses to close ground rapidly from the final flight.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race can neutralise Ripsnorter's positional advantage as the field bunches turning for home and hold-up types with finishing ability get into the race without losing ground; the final 2f then becomes a flat sprint where horses with the best recent form and freshness can prevail.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and Ripsnorter or Menas Miracle prove too fit and sharp for the field to reel in.
scenarios.body: A strong gallop on Good ground over 2m2f at Downpatrick will expose hold-up types who are navigating a congested midfield; horses who have secured their natural position from the outset are insulated from traffic and energy-waste.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Each-Way Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the congested and overpopulated midfield creates significant interference or jumping errors that disrupt the closers' runs and deliver the race to an outsider who threads through cleanly.
scenarios.body: With so many horses redistibuted into the middle of the race, even minor jumping trouble can cause a pile-up effect that unsettles fancied hold-up horses and hands a clean passage to one with shrewd jockeyship; this scenario is low probability precisely because it requires external misfortune rather than a naturally-occurring pace shape.

watchPoints.text: Menas Miracle (Mr B T Stone, 7) is the only prominent type who can sit directly behind Ripsnorter and inherit the race without a fight for position — watch whether he moves smoothly into second turning for home, as that is the precise move that shapes the finish.

The midfield is severely overcrowded with redistributed hold-up types (South Of Killerig, He Who Dares, Granlahan, Banphrionsa Alainn, Firstupbestdressed, John Dixen all competing for the same ground) — watch for interference or checking at hurdles on the far side where the field tightens.

Le Diablo is a strong each-way profile if JJ Slevin can engineer a clean run from off the pace; watch whether he is trapped behind the midfield tangle turning for home, as a blocked passage would cost him his chance in a falsely-run race.

Ripsnorter's jumping at hurdles under pressure is the key variable — he recorded 8th and 10th in his two most recent runs before winning last time; if he makes a significant error at a hurdle under a controlled lead, Menas Miracle or a trailing tracker could seize the initiative earlier than expected.

He Who Dares and Granlahan both "fades in finish" or have modest closing records yet are the two redistributed horses with the most credible recent form (1W2P and 0W3P respectively in similar going) — watch whether either secures a position closer than their natural style would suggest in the early stages, which would be a meaningful upgrade to their winning chance.

races.name: North Down Marquees Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tribal Moon
runners_data.note: Noel Kelly-trained five-year-old who has finished third over 2m2f on Good, showing some ability, but the form string of 0-7305 is modest and the horse's natural hold-up style means it is squeezed into midfield by the volume of closers in this field, reducing its already limited prospects.

runners_data.name: Coded Welder
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer with a second on the form string over 2m3f and consistent placed efforts; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim could be significant over this trip, and tracking the leader from a comfortable pitch suits its profile well in a single-pace race.

runners_data.name: Fortis Et Liber
runners_data.note: The key pace influence — Colin Bowe's five-year-old has one run over hurdles (second at 2m2f on Good) and the style tag confirms it will lead; Ricky Doyle faces no realistic challenger for the front, which is a significant tactical advantage over 2m6f at Good to Good.

runners_data.name: Fuusland
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's lightly raced five-year-old carries obvious class credentials and a fourth on debut over hurdles at 2m2f on Good; its genuine hold-up style pushes it into a congested midfield berth here, meaning it cannot race as naturally as Elliott would want, and 48 days off adds a mild fitness query.

runners_data.name: Majestic Horizon
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's unexposed five-year-old has placed twice from three hurdle starts on Good ground under Darragh O'Keeffe; the unknown style tag reflects limited evidence, 101 days between runs is a minor flag, but the lightly raced profile means significant improvement is plausible at 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Salty Racer
runners_data.note: Noel Kelly runner flagged for fading in the finish, with a single run showing an eighth over 2m on Good; the hold-up profile in a race dominated by closers offers little shape advantage, and the fade tendency at the business end is a concern over this stamina trip.

runners_data.name: Tommy Go Maith
runners_data.note: A string of pulled-up and unseated runs under its belt including over hurdles and chase trips; Thomas McGettigan's five-year-old ran just seven days ago and wears a visor, but the form reading is deeply unpromising and its natural hold-up tendency is further blunted by redistribution into the midfield pack.

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for P J Rothwell with a tendency to fade, having placed just once from five hurdle starts; the 12-day turnaround and a form string of P-8905 over 2m-2m4f on Good gives little encouragement, and the hold-up style will find this pace map unsympathetic.

runners_data.name: Six Mile Suzy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a 223-day absence and three hurdle runs all resulting in double-figure finishes, including an 18th on soft; W J Bryson has a blank 14-day record and the tongue-tie plus the layoff combine to make this a very speculative runner with no shape advantage.

runners_data.name: Ritz Plan
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with placed hurdle form — two seconds on Heavy and one fourth on Good — who should track prominently; J J Slevin is a significant jockey booking, the 47-day break is not alarming, but the Going records skew to softer surfaces and the one Good-ground run produced only a seventh over 2m2f.

races.paceDynamic: Fortis Et Liber is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner maiden hurdle over 2m6f on Good ground at Downpatrick, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Ricky Doyle can dictate an entirely uncontested gallop from the front. Coded Welder and Ritz Plan are the closest things to on-pace rivals, but neither carries the profile to seriously dispute for the lead through the early stages of this stamina test, meaning Fortis Et Liber will control tempo from flag to finish. The field contains a heavy cluster of hold-up types — Tribal Moon, Fuusland, Tommy Go Maith, Salty Racer, Jolly D'olivate, and Six Mile Suzy all prefer to race from the rear — and this glut of closers means the pace map cannot accommodate all of them naturally; those redistributed to midfield are unlikely to find their true position. This race shape strongly favours a horse who can race prominently or win from the front, as a controlled pace over this trip on Good ground typically produces a test of jumping accuracy and stamina rather than a true-run race that rewards deep closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fortis Et Liber Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fortis Et Liber settles comfortably in front and the field trails at a rhythm that suits the pace-setter, never accelerating sharply enough to dislodge it.
scenarios.body: Fortis Et Liber commands every yard at a sustainable tempo, jumping fluently over 2m6f on Good ground with no one willing to take it on, and races clear from the final flight as rivals from the hold-up pack fail to generate enough momentum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Fortis Et Liber fades on the final climb and one of the prominent-tracking horses produces a clean late jump to collar it.
scenarios.body: Coded Welder or Ritz Plan, tracking just off the pace, benefits from a well-judged stalking ride and pounces approaching the final hurdle when the front-runner's stamina is tested over the last half-mile of 2m6f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and a genuine hold-up runner threads through from midfield to catch tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: Even with the pace map congested by redistributed closers, Fuusland or Tribal Moon — carrying the strongest form credentials among the hold-up runners — could benefit if the race is unusually strongly run and the field strings out, though their mapped position away from the rail makes late passage difficult.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Majestic Horizon, lightly raced and unexposed over this longer trip, steps forward significantly on its two previous placed efforts to outclass this field.
scenarios.body: Majestic Horizon has finished third twice at shorter distances on Good ground and its unknown ceiling makes it a plausible improver at 2m6f under Darragh O'Keeffe, though it must demonstrate the extra stamina required and overcome 101 days off the track.

watchPoints.text: Fortis Et Liber's jumping is the single biggest swing factor — a jumping error at any flight could immediately transform the race shape and bring the prominent pair (Coded Welder, Ritz Plan) into play far sooner than expected.

Fuusland and Tribal Moon are both legitimate hold-up horses mapped artificially into midfield by the volume of closers; watch whether either drifts back to find clear air at the rear, which would leave them with an enormous amount of ground to make up in a race controlled at a sustainable tempo.

Majestic Horizon's 101-day break under Darragh O'Keeffe could see it either strip to peak fitness or need the run — watch the betting market late for any clues from the Rothwell yard, who also run Jolly D'olivate in the same race.

Tommy Go Maith ran just seven days ago, has a history of not completing, and wears a visor; it is worth monitoring early to see whether it jumps fluently, as a fall or mistake from this runner in the midfield cluster could cause interference to surrounding horses including the redistributed hold-up types.

Six Mile Suzy's 223-day absence combined with a form line of 0/00- makes it a safety concern from a traffic perspective; if it weakens sharply before the turn in, backmarkers tracking into contention should be aware of its likely position.

races.name: AJC Group Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bruant
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by style but fades in the finish according to the profile note — the 25-day return looks fine and the 2/21f Good run is encouraging for the trip, yet the tendency to weaken late makes this race shape, where closers are disadvantaged, particularly tricky.
runners_data.comment: Bruant shaped well when runner-up last time out and his win three starts back shows he retains the ability to get his head in front; experience over today's going is a further plus, and he arrives here fresh enough on 25 days' rest to make his presence felt.

runners_data.name: Kashchei
runners_data.note: Kevin Healy's claim is notable here and the horse landed a 21f Good ground hurdle last time; a true hold-up type whose natural position at the rear is well-suited to a genuinely run race, though 62 days between runs and a moderate sim-going record (8/13) temper enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Kashchei has run over today's trip and going before, and a win two starts back underlines his claims as the top-rated runner in this field; the main concern is that pulled-up effort last time out, after a 62-day absence now to factor in.

runners_data.name: Cozone
runners_data.note: Sole amateur from Matthew J Smith's yard, nine-year-old with wins on both Good and Soft — 79 days between runs is a long gap, and the hold-up style puts him at a disadvantage given the expected pace scenario; the headgear note (tb) could mean a small bounce in concentration.
runners_data.comment: Cozone won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but 79 days off the track raises a fitness query and 165 lb is a stern burden for a horse ranked midfield in this field.

runners_data.name: Shinnhill
runners_data.note: A 22-day freshen-up brings this nine-year-old back having won over 18f on Good at the same sim-going standard, and the prominent style fits the expected race shape well — the drop back from that 1/7 blot in the form string needs explaining but recent Downpatrick course form is solid.
runners_data.comment: Shinnhill arrives on the back of a second last time out, though a pulled-up effort two starts back clouds his recent profile; he handles today's going and returns after a 22-day break, but ranked seventh of eleven on rating, he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old has been remarkably consistent on Good ground (6/7 sim-going, five placed efforts) and ran just 12 days ago, suggesting Cromwell has him primed — prominent style means he is ideally positioned to chase down the leader from a handy berth.
runners_data.comment: Seven Towers won last time out and arrives just 12 days later in fine trim, with experience of today's going working in his favour; the main risk is that his two runs back showed a sharp drop to ninth, hinting at some inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's six-year-old is a genuine closer by inclination — four placed efforts from nine sim-going runs but no wins on Good, and the style-fit discount (0.92) reflects that it will likely be racing closer to mid-division than its natural rearward comfort zone in this race.
runners_data.comment: Penzance has been knocking on the door, finishing second three times in recent starts, and at 15 days between runs he arrives fresh and fit; rated 114 by us against an official mark of 105, he looks overdue a change of fortune, though his inability to convert remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Tolka Row
runners_data.note: David O'Brien's runner won over 22f on Good ground and carries genuine hold-up form credentials — the style-fit tag (0.93) is the key caveat here, as the surplus of closers means Flanagan will find himself further forward than ideal, blunting what is otherwise a well-credentialled stayer.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but pulled up three starts back, and that inconsistency is the key concern; he has distance and going experience to draw on and returns fit on 17 days' rest, though eighth last time out and a career-high 159 lb test his claims here.

runners_data.name: Down Around
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner won over course and distance on Good ground last time out and carries proven front-running credentials — the uncontested lead is his to lose, and his 13/15 sim-going record underlines how well this surface suits him; blinkers fitted.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Down Around is hard to fancy at the weights, but he does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Tell Nobody Nothin
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's runner returns after 107 days off and, while a course-and-distance win on Good reads encouragingly, the lengthy absence is a significant flag — prominent style suits the shape, but Meade's 14-day record (1/16) suggests timing of this return is carefully planned.
runners_data.comment: Tell Nobody Nothin was a winner two starts back but has since been pulled up, and 107 days on the sidelines plus a rating of 106 ranked tenth of eleven make him very hard to fancy; the experience over today's trip and going is at least a small positive.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Noel Meade also runs this five-year-old, a natural closer with a 1/18f win on Good but more at home at shorter trips — the redistribution to midfield means Meyler faces a positioning compromise, and this trip at 2m6f stretches what has looked best at up to 2m2f.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner three starts back and a close second two starts back shows he retains ability, but 50 days off the track and a stiff 156 lb ask give pause, even if he has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Lightest weight in the race (143lbs) and the most straightforward outsider angle — Daniel King rides and the prominent style is fine, but the OR of 87 against a field rated in the hundreds is a steep class gap that a favourable pace shape alone is unlikely to overcome.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Love Like This makes her case hard to build — unplaced in two of her last three starts, she has run over today's trip and going, and a win does feature in recent form, but that came six starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Down Around is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to press them early, Danny Gilligan can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m6f trip on Good ground — a configuration that historically rewards the horse on the front end at Downpatrick. Shinnhill, Seven Towers, and Tell Nobody Nothin will try to sit prominently behind, creating a small group of chasers but no genuine pressure on the leader. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear: Penzance, Tolka Row, and Mickey Cohen are genuine closers by nature but are redistributed to midfield on this map because Bruant, Kashchei, and Cozone are also true hold-up horses — meaning several of these runners will be racing outside their optimal position. The tactical verdict is clear: a single uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace on a fair surface over a stamina trip strongly favours prominent-to-front types who can travel in the slipstream and quicken at the last, rather than true closers who may find the tempo insufficient to generate the gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Down Around Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around leads uncontested and sets a fair but not punishing gallop, grinding out the field from the front.
scenarios.body: Down Around's recent course-and-distance win on Good ground and Elliott's proven 14-day record give this horse every reason to replicate that front-running display; on 2m6f at Downpatrick, a loose leader who stays on relentlessly is very hard to peg back. The prominent chasers who travel smoothly in behind — Seven Towers and Shinnhill — are best placed to challenge late, but if the leader has enough in reserve, neither may close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around's lead is modest enough that a well-positioned prominent type can surge past from two out.
scenarios.body: Seven Towers has the strongest recent form profile in the prominent group with a run just 12 days ago and consistent good-ground placed efforts, while Shinnhill brings a course win and a fresh 22-day return to form — either can pounce if the pace is just fractionally too slow to test them before the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely brisk enough to string the field out and create space for a late finisher to pick off tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: Tolka Row and Kashchei are the most likely beneficiaries among the hold-up types, with Tolka Row boasting a course-distance win on identical going and Kashchei holding a recent hurdle win; however, both are mapped to positions outside their natural rearward role, making this shape harder to execute than it appears on paper. This scenario requires a tempo that simply isn't expected with only one front-runner — it remains a minority chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset From The Weights
scenarios.trigger: If the race collapses into a messy, slowly-run bunched finish where the lower-weighted horses benefit from the handicap margin.
scenarios.body: Love Like This or Mickey Cohen, carrying the lightest burdens in the field, could benefit if the race turns tactical and the finish becomes a sprint that nullifies the class advantage of the higher-rated runners. Mickey Cohen's best form has come fresh at a mile-and-a-half to two miles rather than this stamina test, but at this weight it cannot be entirely dismissed.

watchPoints.text: Down Around's uncontested lead is the defining factor — if Danny Gilligan takes a firm hold early and dictates a slow first half, the race could turn into a sprint finish that undermines horses rated on a genuine gallop.

Tell Nobody Nothin returns from 107 days off — watch the market move for this Noel Meade runner, as a sharp market move would suggest connections are confident despite the layoff, which would significantly change the prominent-shape dynamic.

Penzance, Tolka Row, and Mickey Cohen are all genuine closers likely to find themselves further forward than natural — if they bunch behind the leader mid-race, they risk burning energy early and compromising their finish, creating interference risk at hurdles.

Seven Towers ran just 12 days ago for a trainer (Cromwell) who fires them fit second time — a low-key recent effort followed by a quick return is a recognisable Cromwell pattern worth monitoring in the market before the off.

Kashchei's jockey Kevin Healy (7lb claim) reduces what is already a low weight — at 62 days since last run on a going that suits, watch if the claim makes this horse an each-way price that the market underestimates against the more exposed runners.

races.name: Cosy Group Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Barton Sky
runners_data.note: A genuinely patient hold-up operator for Hanlon, returning off 21 days with sound course form on good ground, though restricted to just two recent runs and both outside the placings; the horse's true rearward style is unlikely to be accommodated in a seven-runner beginners' chase with prominent types dominating the shape, temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Barton Sky arrives winless in his last four starts, with a pulled-up effort three starts back doing little to inspire confidence, and he ranks last on our figures here — though a second four starts back shows he can compete, and 21 days off should leave him fresh.

runners_data.name: Jabbar
runners_data.note: Thomas O'Connor's 7lb claim is the headline angle for Gerard O'Leary's handler, but a hold-up horse with a moderate 0W3P record on similar going and wide-margin beaten efforts at 17f in his last two starts raises serious stamina questions at this trip and in this configuration.
runners_data.comment: Jabbar has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second twice and third once in his last four, and with 24 days between runs he arrives fresh; the main risk is that he remains yet to win.

runners_data.name: Kevin's Pride
runners_data.note: McConnell's seven-year-old is a genuine prominent racer with two wins and three places from nine similar-going starts, and the tongue-tie remains in place; stepping back from 26f to 2m3½f is a clear asset, and the 5lb claim of Eoghan Finegan keeps the weight manageable — form figures of 14-54 mask a horse who is consistently competitive off a break.
runners_data.comment: Kevin's Pride landed a winner four starts back and has experience of today's trip and going to call on, making him a genuine threat at 166 lb; the main risk is that 52 days off the track leaves his current sharpness an open question.

runners_data.name: Killeemore Lad
runners_data.note: Philip Donovan rides a course-and-distance fit horse in fine recent form, with three consecutive seconds before a fall at odds-on last time; Slattery's runner is 10/15 on similar going with six placings and has won over course-and-distance — a fluent jumper who will be prominent and is the most consistent placegetter in the field.
runners_data.comment: Consistent to a fault, Killeemore Lad has finished second in four of his last five completed starts and, fit from a run 18 days ago with experience over today's trip and conditions, his profile warrants plenty of respect despite being yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Robbies Rock
runners_data.note: Cromwell's five-year-old is the youngest in the race and brings a tongue-tie plus three wins from 15 similar-going starts, but his natural style is closer-to-hold-up and he has form figures of 8 and 8 in his most recent outings; if he gets close enough to the tempo he is a live each-way contender, though his best performance (14f win) came at shorter.
runners_data.comment: Robbies Rock caught the eye with a second two starts back and knows today's going, giving him a solid platform at 166 lb; the worry is that eighth last time out suggests he can be frustratingly inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Spinola Bay
runners_data.note: Elliott's six-year-old carries hood and is the most experienced prominent racer in the field with a 1W2P record on good ground from six starts, winning twice over 16f; a return to the right trip after a disappointing 7th last time and the first-time hood strongly suggests the yard expects a bounce-back, making him one of the more interesting pace-shape beneficiaries.
runners_data.comment: Spinola Bay showed a good turn of form when winning back-to-back three and four starts back, but has disappointed in his last two outings, and 41 days off the track plus a hefty 166 lb burden make him hard to fancy with confidence despite going experience and a rating of 108.

runners_data.name: Herja
runners_data.note: Griffin's mare is a confirmed front-runner who has placed in 9 of 13 career starts with excellent course-and-trip suitability (13/15 similar-going runs), and the tongue-tie applied for this beginners' drop in class could sharpen her early; Harry Sexton's 7lb claim keeps her competitive at the weights and an uncontested lead over inexperienced rivals is a significant tactical gift.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Herja is hard to fancy despite her consistency — three runner-up finishes in recent starts show she tries hard, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but 159 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

races.paceDynamic: Herja is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only seven runners in a beginners' chase, is almost certain to bowl along uncontested from the front under Harry Sexton. The pace she sets should be honest rather than frantic — a controlled gallop on good ground over 2m3½f that keeps the race together rather than stringing it out, meaning those tracking her will be well positioned to pounce. Prominent types Kevin's Pride, Killeemore Lad, and Spinola Bay are best placed to exploit this shape, sitting close to the tempo and launching their challenges at the final fences. The field carries more hold-up runners (Barton Sky, Jabbar, Robbies Rock) than the map can naturally accommodate at the rear, and Barton Sky in particular is a genuine hold-up horse who is mapped to midfield but unlikely to secure that position in practice; of the three, Robbies Rock — the youngest and most athletically capable — is the most likely to get close enough to be competitive. This race shape firmly favours horses who can travel prominently, conserve energy tracking a lone leader, and jump fluently at speed — the prominent racer who jumps best and pings the last will almost certainly dictate the finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Herja Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Herja sets a controlled solo pace and a prominent tracker jumps fluently to collar her at the last.
scenarios.body: Herja's uncontested lead sets a manageable gallop that keeps the race together, allowing Kevin's Pride, Killeemore Lad, or Spinola Bay to sit a length or two off the pace, conserve energy over fences, and deliver a clean challenge jumping the last. Prominent types with sound jumping and good ground form are rewarded directly, as the race is not run to suit grinders or closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Herja Sticks On
scenarios.trigger: If Herja's controlled front-running is so accurate and economical that no prominent horse can close the gap after the last.
scenarios.body: Herja, dropped significantly in class with a tongue-tie applied, finds the beginners' company much easier than recent starts and her bold jumping at a steady tempo costs pursuers their chance to narrow the margin. A 7lb-claiming jockey keeping things unhurried from the front means she is never wasteful of energy, and prominent horses who need a stronger gallop to come past are left unable to mount a meaningful challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough mid-race to tire prominent horses and leave room for a late rattle from a hold-up type.
scenarios.body: Should Spinola Bay or Killeemore Lad push forward to test Herja, lifting the gallop through the middle section, hold-up runners who are conserving energy in rear positions could find the leaders tying up at the final fence. Robbies Rock, with a win and place at similar trips on good ground, is best credentialed here, though Barton Sky racing out of its preferred role makes this scenario less reliable than the probability suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Jumping Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fencing errors among the prominent pack disrupt the race shape and hand the initiative to a surviving stalker.
scenarios.body: In a beginners' chase with seven inexperienced chasers, any cluster of jumping errors at key fences could eliminate prominent contenders mid-race, turning a structured contest into a scramble for survival. The horse that jumps cleanest regardless of position wins, and Killeemore Lad's consistent placed form and recent course fitness give marginal edge in chaos.

watchPoints.text: Herja's jumping accuracy is the pivotal variable — if she makes a serious error at any of the early fences her race is over and the entire predicted shape collapses, handing initiative to whoever is tracking her most closely.

Killeemore Lad fell last time out in a race he was well fancied for; watch for any signs of jumping hesitancy or loss of confidence at the early fences that could see him detach from the prominent group before the race enters its decisive phase.

Spinola Bay's headgear change (first-time hood for Elliott) is worth monitoring in the paddock and at the start — if it sharpens him too much and he contests the early lead with Herja rather than tracking her, the pace could quicken sharply and compromise prominent horses who need a steadier tempo.

Barton Sky and Jabbar as hold-up types in a small-field beginners' chase over fences may find themselves trapped on the rail in traffic if the prominent pack sets a steady pace — positional awareness of their starting berths and early manoeuvring is worth noting before the tape rises.

races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Driveonwill
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer at OR 100 — the highest-rated horse in the field — trained by Ross O'Sullivan with Donagh Meyler riding; Good-ground form is solid (sim-going 8/15, one win, one place) and 34 days between runs is fine, but from a hold-up position in a strongly-run race he needs a lot to go right over an unfamiliar trip.|
runners_data.comment: Driveonwill landed a win three starts back and has distance and going experience in his favour, but unplaced on his return 34 days ago and a trainer cold at 0/21 over the past fortnight are real negatives for the 168 lb-burdened gelding.

runners_data.name: Gorthill
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with solid Good-ground course form (10/11 similar-going) and recent run just 10 days ago; at OR 99 and age 10 he is not without stamina questions at 2m3½f but knows this job and will aim to dictate — the danger is Annarubyrose forcing him into a pace duel he cannot sustain.|
runners_data.comment: Gorthill arrives on the back of a second last time out, returning quickly on a surface and trip he has encountered before, and our rating of 116 puts him clear of his 15 rivals — though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Kalsman
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins and four places on similar going (11/15), recently won over 20f on Good and fits the trip; OR 97 and handicap mark look workable if he travels comfortably just off the leaders — arguably the most naturally positioned horse in the field for this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Kalsman arrives in decent nick after consecutive thirds, giving him a placed thread through recent starts, though he was unplaced three starts back and his rating of 94 leaves him ranked seventh of sixteen. Has run over today's trip and going, and 22 days since his last run suggests he's fresh enough to go again.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with consistent form at this trip on Good ground, placed three times in last four completions; jockey Daniel King gives a 7lb claim here which is meaningful at this weight, and the horse's Good-ground figures (8/12 similar going) are encouraging — needs the pace to set up a finish.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Run For The Border nonetheless shows consistent placing form — third last time out and a second three starts back — and has run over today's trip and going before, though 163 lb is the significant concern against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Full Noise
runners_data.note: Prominent racer at OR 94 with Good-ground form and two career wins; the 7lb claim for Mr D McGill is a useful weight reduction and his hg:p headgear flags he needs covering early — if settled behind the duelling leaders he could travel powerfully into contention.|
runners_data.comment: Full Noise shaped well when third last time out and was second three starts back, and he has distance and going experience to call on carrying 162 lb; the risk is that he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Wing Back
runners_data.note: Hold-up type at OR 93 carrying a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag, which is a significant concern in a strong-pace scenario where the closing run may arrive too late; 45 days off the track adds a fitness query despite one win and two places on Good.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Wing Back at least brings distance and going experience to the table, though a sixth last time out and a string of disappointing efforts before that make it hard to see him troubling the leaders from a rating of 93 carrying 161 lb.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer at OR 90 trained by John Joseph Hanlon, a handler with two winners in 15-day trainer form; recent run 17 days ago keeps fitness ticking and his Good-ground record (8/15) is modest — best of three runs here has been a second, and the crowded prominent group may squeeze his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but a second two starts back suggests he retains ability, and having run over today's trip and going is a plus; the 158 lb burden may test his resolution here.

runners_data.name: Our Zebo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but genuinely strong on Good going — 12/15 similar-going runs, three wins and seven places; recent run 10 days ago at OR 89 and the trip (22f wins) supports the step up to today's 2m3½f — Conor Stone-Walsh has to plot a path from further back than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Our Zebo won three starts back and was placed twice more in that same sequence, arriving here fit on a quick ten-day turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour; the concern is that his last two efforts produced a sixth and a seventh, suggesting he may need to find more.

runners_data.name: My Policy
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer whose true racing style sits further back than the map position suggests; trainer Patrick Rooney has 0/1 in the 14-day window and the horse has pulled up twice in recent form — the redistribution to midfield still leaves it needing a big swing in pace to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts — with two consecutive pulls and 153 lb to carry — she does bring going experience to the table, though a return to form looks a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Returned from a series of non-completions to win last time out (OR 85), trained by W J Lanigan with J J Slevin booked — a significant jockey upgrade; hg:p headgear and Good-going form (8/10) are positives, and Slevin's tactical awareness could extract a forward move from what is technically a hold-up profile.|
runners_data.comment: Not So Serious showed smart form when winning two starts back, and our rating of 101 makes him a serious threat off a light 153 lb on going he has experience of; the unseating last time is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: King's Son
runners_data.note: Prominent-style chaser at OR 84 with a modest recent record (6, 6, 6, 3, 15 in last five), placed just once on Good; Philip Donovan rides and the horse's 8/10 similar-going record is serviceable but the form trajectory is not encouraging in a competitive 16-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three consecutive finishes no better than sixth the concern, King's Son does bring distance-and-going experience and returns after a fair 27-day break, though a rating of 88 leaves him facing a stiff ask from 11th in the rankings.

runners_data.name: The Cobblers Wife
runners_data.note: Won last time out (OR 82) and Danny Mullins takes the ride — an eye-catching combination — but her natural running style is hold-up and she's pushed toward midfield by the crowded map; with only 3/9 runs on Good going she is less proven in these conditions than her recent win might suggest.|
runners_data.comment: The Cobblers Wife won last time out but that masks a patchy recent profile, and with our rating 8 lb below her official mark she looks to have plenty to find against these rivals; the distance and going hold no fears at least.

runners_data.name: Deadheat
runners_data.note: A 13-year-old at OR 79 whose best recent effort was a third at 26f on Good; a genuine hold-up type whose pace-dependent style is further compromised by age and the necessity of racing out of position in a fast-run race — best treated with caution despite the Good-ground profile.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a pulled up and a ninth among recent efforts, Deadheat is hard to fancy from 12th in the ratings; he has run over today's trip and going before, and ten days since his third last time out at least suggests fitness.

runners_data.name: Nobody
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag and no wins or places in five career starts; the combination of inexperience, a genuine hold-up style pushed into midfield, and a claim for Josh Williamson (3) makes this one of the least likely winners in the field based on current evidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Nobody makes little appeal here — an unseating last time out compounds the concern, though he has run over today's going before and 15 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Baltinglass Hill
runners_data.note: 110 days off the track is the dominant concern here — returning from a long absence in a 16-runner competitive handicap chase on Good ground at OR 73; Simon Torrens rides for PJ Rothwell whose 14-day strike rate is 3/19, but the layoff alone warrants a significant discount until fitness is proven.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two pull-ups among them, Baltinglass Hill arrives after a 110-day absence and is ranked well below the field on our figures, making him very hard to fancy despite having experience of today's trip and going and carrying 141 lb.

runners_data.name: Annarubyrose
runners_data.note: The other declared front-runner, five-year-old with all five recent runs on Good ground at Downpatrick, so track-fit; her OR of 88 leaves her giving weight to Gorthill and at this distance the pace contest may drain her before the finish.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 13 of 16 on our figures, Annarubyrose faces a stiff task under 156 lb, though experience on today's going and a second four starts back offer slim crumbs of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Gorthill and Annarubyrose are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from flag to first fence, creating a genuinely contested gallop over 2m3½f on Good ground at Downpatrick — a track where pace is rarely slow. With both horses intent on leading, the tempo should be honest to strong throughout, compressing the race and reducing the scope for late-closers to manufacture a sweeping finish. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the duelling front pair, travel comfortably, and pounce when one or both leaders capitulate — horses like Kalsman, Full Noise, and My Cullen are ideally positioned to exploit that scenario. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can honestly place at the rear; My Policy, The Cobblers Wife, Deadheat, and Nobody are all genuine hold-up performers redistributed toward midfield on the map — in reality, the contested pace makes their true position even further back, limiting their prospects of delivering a winning challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Collide, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gorthill and Annarubyrose burn each other out disputing the lead and a prominent tracker pounces from the third fence.
scenarios.body: The duel between Gorthill and Annarubyrose sets a fierce gallop that leaves both vulnerable from two out, handing the race to a relaxed, prominent mover who has tracked the pace without expending energy; Good ground at Downpatrick suits handy, jump-efficient chasers who can capitalise at the top of the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Gorthill — gains a clear advantage early and is allowed to control the tempo unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Gorthill has strong course form on Good going and, if Annarubyrose fails to sustain the duel or fades after the first circuit, Gorthill could dictate at a more sustainable clip and prove very difficult to peg back; experienced front-runners who can jump cleanly and conserve energy once in command are the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong it implodes the front group and a horse tracking in the first half of midfield — not from the back — delivers a well-timed challenge.
scenarios.body: Our Zebo and Driveonwill, both horses with form on Good ground who are capable of travelling through the race without being far back, could find the carnage in front creating an opening that rewards a well-timed run from mid-division; this scenario is plausible but depends on the front pair running freely enough to set up a true finish, which is not guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unsustainably hot from the outset and the entire prominent group fades, leaving a genuine back-marker to sweep through.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally less likely because the horses best suited to it — My Policy, The Cobblers Wife, Deadheat, Nobody — are all redistributed away from their natural positions and will be even further back in a fast-run race than the map suggests; the combination of contested pace and their forced deep position makes a winning late challenge improbable rather than impossible.

watchPoints.text: Gorthill and Annarubyrose will lock horns from the first fence — watch which of the two establishes a clear lead by the second fence; if neither gives way the tempo could be race-ruinously fast and eliminate both as winning prospects.

Kalsman jumped to the head of market interest for good reason — watch his jumping at the early fences, as any mistake under Kieren Buckley while racing prominently in a fast-run race could cost him position he cannot recover.

The Cobblers Wife's booking of Danny Mullins is a market mover in waiting — watch the market moves pre-race, as Mullins rarely accepts a ride in a 16-runner handicap chase without believing the horse is primed despite the going question.

Not So Serious returned to form with a win last time and J J Slevin represents a notable jockey upgrade — monitor whether Slevin attempts to push forward earlier than the horse's natural style suggests, which would signal a positional plan change.

Baltinglass Hill's 110-day absence in a race of this size is a flag for the entire field — if he shows any early signs of blowing up or jumping poorly it confirms fitness concerns and removes a variable from the shape entirely.

races.name: Downpatrick Racecourse Style Awards Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: OR 121 top-weight holder in fine going form (sim-going 14/15), but Harry Sexton's 7lb claim is offset by a heavy 167lbs burden; this is a genuine hold-up horse and on a Downpatrick circuit where a controlled Finnians Row is unlikely to lay down the gallop needed, covering the ground late will be a tall order.|
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and in solid form despite being winless in his last six, War Correspondent brings distance and going experience into this and rates four pounds clear of his rivals on our figures, making him the one to beat off 167 lb.

runners_data.name: Beggars Rock
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 19f on Good and carries Kevin Sexton at 159lbs; bred to stay and handles this ground well (11/15 sim-going), but finishing from off the pace is genuinely his style and a moderate front-runner's tempo here is his biggest enemy.|
runners_data.comment: Beggars Rock showed he can win in his last five starts, scoring most recently, though he was unplaced the run before and our rating of 107 leaves him with something to prove against the top-rated runners; the 159 lb burden is no help either.

runners_data.name: Stuntman Steve
runners_data.note: 58 days off the track for Gavin Cromwell, who has a live yard (5/35 in 14 days); a true rear-of-field operator, Eoghan Finegan's 5lb claim is useful but the horse's natural rear-running inclination cannot express itself properly in a race with only one genuine pace-setter setting a sedate tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Stuntman Steve has experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 118 suggests he holds strong claims as a leading danger here; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and his interrupted run of form — including an unseating and a pulled up — gives cause for caution.

runners_data.name: Finnians Row
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins (1-1) on Good ground with sim-going record of 13/15 and four wins in his last six sim-going appearances; the lone confirmed leader who will set a sustainable gallop unchallenged — absolutely the horse the race revolves around, and Niall Moore's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable at 153lbs.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and carrying a hefty 153 lb, Finnias Row is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins two and three starts back, as he was unplaced last time out and has not always completed in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Piccolo Player
runners_data.note: Youngest runner in the field at five years old with modest sim-going figures (5/13) and no wins; Daniel King has no claim and the horse's natural position at the rear of the field is squeezed out by so many hold-up types — its chances rest on a pace collapse that looks improbable.|
runners_data.comment: Piccolo Player has been knocking at the door, finishing third in each of his last two starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before — the concern is whether he can finally convert that consistency into a winning effort carrying a hefty 150 lb.

runners_data.name: Presenting Lad
runners_data.note: Back within 15 days, Phillip Enright takes over for Mark McNiff; placed twice over this 16f trip on Good (2,2) and showed a late run recently, though structurally this race shape forces him further forward than he wants to be, which tempers confidence in his closing ability.|
runners_data.comment: Presenting Lad was second last time out and has run over today's trip and going, his overall profile suggesting he retains solid claims here — yet the pulled-up run two starts back remains the one question mark connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Rightfolksplease
runners_data.note: Three wins from his last five on Good ground at 16f, Kevin Healy's 7lb claim brings him down to 147lbs and represents genuine value in the saddle; the natural beneficiary if Finnians Row fades, and his stalking style slots in perfectly just behind the leader without needing to race out of role.|
runners_data.comment: Rightfolksplease arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures he faces a stiff ask against stronger company here, and 147 lb is no help.

races.paceDynamic: Finnians Row is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner handicap chase and, crucially, faces no meaningful pace pressure — Rightfolksplease will track from a prominent position but is not a natural challenger for the lead, meaning Finnians Row can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop over the 2m2f Downpatrick trip on Good ground. With Finnians Row in career-best form (back-to-back wins, sim-going record of 13/15), an uncontested lead at a sensible tempo is almost certain, and the Good ground will allow him to travel fluently without burning out his stamina reserves. The four hold-up horses — War Correspondent, Beggars Rock, Stuntman Steve, and Piccolo Player — will be forced to give chunks of ground to the pace-setter if the gallop remains measured, which on this tight track with limited run-in suits a horse who can control from the front. This race shape emphatically favours the lone front-runner and horses with genuine prominent/stalking ability; true hold-up types face an uphill task closing on a controlled tempo around Downpatrick's tight configuration. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can honestly place at the rear — Stuntman Steve, Piccolo Player, and Presenting Lad are redistributed to midfield positions they would not naturally command, and it is Rightfolksplease who is most likely to genuinely secure a close-up berth to Finnians Row.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Finnians Row Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Finnians Row jumps cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead, controlling tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Niall Moore dictates the pace and can conserve his mount's energy through the early stages, presenting a fresh galloping threat from the last fence; Finnians Row's back-to-back wins on matching Good ground confirm he is in the form of his life and this scenario is his race to lose.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Rightfolksplease tracks the pace efficiently and picks up powerfully after the last fence to overhaul a tiring Finnians Row.
scenarios.body: Rightfolksplease has won three of his last five starts at this trip and going combination, and Kevin Healy's 7lb claim keeps the weight competitive; if Finnians Row sets a fraction too strong a gallop in the middle sector, Rightfolksplease is ideally placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave true hold-up horses with a meaningful target to aim at late.
scenarios.body: War Correspondent and Beggars Rock are the most credible closers with the class figures to cover ground quickly; however, Downpatrick's track configuration and a likely moderate tempo make this scenario structurally unlikely, and both would need the pace to be materially faster than Finnians Row has shown any inclination to set.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Leader Fades Early
scenarios.trigger: If Finnians Row makes a jumping error or is pressured unexpectedly and the race deteriorates into a messy scramble.
scenarios.body: Presenting Lad's recent second at this distance on Good ground and Beggars Rock's course form give them an outside path if the race loses its shape entirely; this scenario is low probability given Finnians Row's jumping record but is not impossible for a 10-year-old over fences.

watchPoints.text: Watch Finnians Row at the first fence — a jumping error for the sole pace-setter could collapse the entire race structure and open it to Beggars Rock and Presenting Lad.

Rightfolksplease's jockey Kevin Healy (7lb claim) is relatively inexperienced — watch for whether he gets Rightfolksplease into a natural stalking position or gets shuffled back into the pack, which would significantly reduce his chance.

War Correspondent at 167lbs is the heaviest carrier in the field; if he travels less than fluently in the middle stages, his hold-up style offers minimal compensation at a venue where the run-in is tight.

Stuntman Steve's 58-day absence for an in-form Gavin Cromwell yard (5/35) is worth monitoring on-course — if the horse shows signs of freshness in the paddock it could surprise, but the race shape does not set up naturally for a hold-up type.

Presenting Lad's quick turnaround (15 days) and jockey change to Enright is worth tracking — if connections have deliberately targeted this race knowing the hold-up position is compromised, a prominently-ridden switch would be a significant market move to note.
